sources.entry: ThenGenerator - Xcode Source Editor Extension for 'Then'

summary.one_liner: ThenGenerator is an Xcode Source Editor Extension that generates "Then"-style Swift UI-object setup code for a selected variable name.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes an Xcode Source Editor Extension that generates code for the selected variable name in Xcode's editor. You enter a variable name without the UI prefix, with a class suffix such as "VariableName + Label" to pick the UIKit class (the example given is a UILabel named repoNameLabel), then select it and run Editor > ThenGenerator > Generate Then Code. A companion app, ThenGeneratorApp, lets you turn individual UIKit classes on or off. The README says the project is built with SwiftUI and stores settings in UserDefaults. It also mentions Xcodegen support and explains how to add new properties by editing model and component view files. Demo images are referenced but not described in text.
use_cases: generate UIKit view setup code in Xcode
create UILabel or other UI objects from a variable name
add a keyboard shortcut for code generation in Xcode
toggle which UIKit classes the generator supports
extend Then-style property templates for iOS code
how_to_run: Install ThenGenerator (the README's Install section is empty; see the project's releases or build instructions)
Enable the extension: System Preferences > Extensions > check ThenGenerator
Select a variable name in Xcode, then choose Editor > ThenGenerator > Generate Then Code
Optional: add a shortcut under Xcode Preferences > Key Bindings by searching ThenGenerator
Optional: launch ThenGeneratorApp to turn UIKit classes on or off
For development: clone the repo and run xcodegen generate
notable: Generates code from a variable name plus a class-type suffix, such as VariableName + Label
Runs from the Xcode Editor menu and can be bound to a custom keyboard shortcut
Companion app ThenGeneratorApp lets you enable or disable UIKit classes
Extensible: add a property by editing a Model file and a Component view file
caveats: Requires macOS 11.0 (Big Sur) or later, per the README
Install section in the README is empty, so setup steps are unclear
The README does not state a license
keywords: generate ui code from variable name
